newsitem.title: UK: Expectations of broad EMU edge down -JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Expectations of broad EMU edge down -JP Morgan.

text.p: Expectations that a broad group of countries will launch the planned single European currency in 1999 were steady to lower in the past week, prices monitored by JP Morgan showed on Friday.

The chances of Ireland joining Germany in European economic and monetary union posted the biggest decline, dipping by 15 percentage points to 62 percent, according to JP Morgan's "EMU calculator" which is derived from the interest-rate swaps market.

The chances of Italy and Spain joining EMU were unchanged at 72 percent and 76 percent respectively. The probability of France and Belgium founding EMU was also unchanged from last week at 100 percent.
Finland and Sweden both registered a decline of three percentage points to 76 percent and 65 percent respectively.
Britain is still viewed as the least likely country to join EMU at its start and its probability of membership slipped to 29 percent from 33 percent a week ago.
JP Morgan said there was a reasonable margin of error in overall probability levels of less than five percentage points on average.
The probabilities are derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU were not a factor, and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
